Subject: Post-call: long-context evals & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today, Peter — really appreciated the walkthrough of your long-doc summarization workload and the examples you shared. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

- Goal: validate model fit for Acme's 50k–200k token documents (legal contracts + research reports) focusing on: truncation behavior, summarization fidelity, and coherent reference retention across sections.
- Recommended models to evaluate (shortlist):
  * redwood-long-13b-v1 (native long-window optimized) — good latency/cost balance for early POC
  * redwood-long-70b-quant (quantized variant) — higher quality for complex summarization; expect higher memory but we can test 2x latency profile
  * llama2-70b-chat-64k (baseline open model) — to match your internal benchmarks

Deliverables I’ll share in this thread: prompt sets for the three evaluation tiers (summaries, Q&A over context, change-delta detection), a benchmark template CSV, and an eval plan doc with expected metrics (ROUGE/chrF, human rating rubric, truncation failure mode taxonomy). See attachments.

Next steps / asks from Acme:
1) Share a small representative sample (3–5 documents) that you’re comfortable sharing for POC (we can sign an NDA if needed).
2) Confirm target SLOs: preferred max p99 latency per request and acceptable token cost per 10k tokens.
3) Tell us whether we should prioritize absolute fidelity (high cost model) or throughput/cost.

Operationally we can spin up a protected evaluation pool under your org (Dedicated or private VPC) — Dev is looped in to propose a quick benchmark schedule and to run initial truncation stress tests.

Links for reference: evaluation plan (Drive) and a small Colab that demonstrates truncation tests.

Cheers,

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: long-context evals & next steps

Thanks for the great questions, Peter. A few quick technical clarifications from the infra side:

- Model quality vs size: expect the 70B quant variant to outperform the 13B on abstractive summarization and cross-section reference resolution, particularly on longer-range dependencies. The 13B long is optimized for larger windows via attention kernels and is surprisingly strong on extraction and cost-effective summarization, but it will show more regressions on nuanced coherence and citation hallucination. We recommend running both as A/B so you can quantify tradeoffs.

- Truncation strategies: we typically test three approaches:
  1) Prefix-preserve + rolling window for the end (keep intro + most recent sections)
  2) Chunk + hierarchical summarization (summarize chunks then summarize summaries)
  3) KV-cache stitching with explicit long-range retrieval for cited sections (best for dereferencing citations)

For a 150k doc with a 64k model window we suggest: chunk & hierarchical summarization for a fidelity-first POC, and an experiment using KV-cache stitching + retrieval for the Q&A workflow. We'll provide an automated stress test that simulates truncation modes and outputs failure-mode flags (e.g., lost-references, section-contradiction, hallucinated-citations).

- Cost: rough hosted API ballparks (USD per 100k input+output tokens):
  * redwood-long-13b-v1: $120
  * redwood-long-70b-quant: $720
  * llama2-70b-chat-64k: $400

I'll queue up a quick benchmark plan and a Colab that showcases truncation tests. If you share the 4 redacted docs via Drive, we can start in the next 48 hours.

—Dev
